period: # Rupees per US dollar
# period   CY    a calendar year          2024
#          FY    an Indian financial year 2024-25   (April 2024 - March 2025)
#          MONTH a calendar month         2024-07
# basis    CY | FY | MONTH
# inr_per_usd  The average reference rate for that period. Blank = not supplied.
# status   verified  a rate taken from a citable published table
#          supplied  a rate you entered yourself; treated as usable
#          needed    the period is used by the dashboard but has no rate yet
# source   Where the number came from. Required for verified and supplied.
# note     Anything a reader should know about that particular rate.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#   Every figure in the dashboard is stored in US dollars
#   both UN Comtrade and the DGCIS export are denominated. The rupee view is a
#   conversion
basis: and a conversion is only as defensible as the rate behind it.

period: #   A single fixed rate applied across thirty years of data would be worse than
#   useless - it would make an exchange-rate movement look like a trade
#   movement. So each period converts at its own average rate
#   used is carried into the published snapshot and shown on the page.
# THE CONVENTION
#   One published period average per row
#   authoritative for its own basis and never mixed inside one basis:
#   CY     World Bank WDI series PA.NUS.FCRF
#          US$
#          Statistics. This is a published calendar-year average
#          the Comtrade calendar-year figures need. The Economic Survey does not
#          publish one
basis: which is why it is not the source here.

period: #   MONTH  FRED series EXINUS
basis: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

period: #   FY     Economic Survey Statistical Appendix Table 5.4
#          average reference rate - the same basis FED already uses in
#          Sectoral_Debt_INR_to_USD.xlsx (see sources/). Indian financial years
#          are a DGCIS/tariff-line concept and only tariff lines use them.
#   A calendar year converts at its calendar-year rate and a month at its own
#   month's rate. Nothing is ever converted at a neighbouring period's rate.
# FAILS CLOSED
#   A period with no rate is not converted. The dashboard shows dollars for it
#   and says the rate is missing; it never falls back to a neighbouring year
#   never interpolates
basis: and never carries a rate forward. Run

period: #       python pipeline/fx.py --report
#   to list the periods the current snapshot needs
#       python pipeline/fx.py --template
#   to append blank rows for the missing ones so they can be filled in.
# The six financial-year rates below are the ones already verified in the FED
# workbook. Everything else is deliberately absent rather than guessed.

source: World Bank WDI PA.NUS.FCRF (official exchange rate, LCU per US$, period average; underlying source IMF International Financial Statistics)
